name: Reliance Industries Ltd
about: Reliance was founded by Dhirubhai Ambani and is now promoted and managed by his elder son, Mukesh Dhirubhai Ambani. Ambani's family has about 50% shareholding in the conglomerate.

statements.text: Revenue compounded 17.8% a year over 5 years (FY21→FY26); profit after tax 12.2%.
EBITDA margin held roughly flat over 5 years (17.3% → 17.0%).
Revenue growth accelerated from 10% to 30% YoY over the last 4 quarters.
Over 5 years: ₹398,016 cr of profit, ₹755,290 cr of operating cash — conversion 1.90x.

ledger.quote: We are not changing ours that is the target that we are going for.
ledger.statement: Retail EBITDA doubling target over about two years reaffirmed
ledger.speaker: Dinesh Taluja
ledger.evidence: Retail EBITDA doubling target reaffirmed in Q2 FY27 ('We are not changing ours'). The facts contain no Retail EBITDA. The ledger frames the horizon as about two years, while Q1 FY27 said three (G8), so the horizon is unclear.

ledger.quote: our module capacity is now six plus gigawatt, and we will be achieving up to 20 gigawatt early next year.
ledger.statement: Solar module capacity to reach 20 GW early CY2027
ledger.speaker: Karan Suri
ledger.evidence: Module capacity is now 6+ GW, with 20 GW guided for early CY2027, so it must more than triple in about one to two quarters. No later update exists.

ledger.quote: we will be achieving again 20-gigawatt capacity sometime first half next year.
ledger.statement: Solar cell capacity to reach 20 GW in H1 CY2027
ledger.speaker: Karan Suri
ledger.evidence: Solar cell capacity to reach 20 GW 'sometime first half next year' (H1 CY2027). The deadline has not arrived. This is a later date than the Q4 FY26 promise of commissioning the cell factory within 'next few quarters' (G9).

ledger.quote: in next half year we will commission our BESS facility, which is a pack and container up to 40-gigawatt hour
ledger.statement: BESS pack and container facility up to 40 GWh commissioned in H1 CY2027
ledger.speaker: Karan Suri
ledger.evidence: BESS pack-and-container facility of up to 40 GWh due in H1 CY2027. No progress data is given.

ledger.quote: we will see the revenues for FY2028 from the new energy complex
ledger.statement: New energy complex to start generating revenue in FY28
ledger.speaker: Karan Suri
ledger.evidence: New energy revenue is guided for FY28. C2 adds that grid connectivity is due in Q1 CY2027 and that the first module was not yet installed at the Q2 FY27 call.

ledger.quote: the ceiling price is expected to go up by at least a dollar
ledger.statement: KGD6 gas ceiling price to rise by at least USD 1 in H2FY27
ledger.speaker: Meeting Audio
ledger.evidence: KGD6 ceiling price to rise by at least USD1 in H2 FY27. H2 began in October 2026 and the Q2 FY27 passages give no price update.

ledger.quote: we expect in the second half the prices to go up
ledger.statement: Realised gas prices to rise in H2FY27, reflecting elevated energy and commodity prices
ledger.speaker: Meeting Audio
ledger.evidence: Realised gas prices are expected to rise in H2 FY27. H2 is in progress and no realised-price data is given.

ledger.quote: It is a target that we are taking that is our ambition
ledger.statement: Target of 2x EBITDA over the next three years (management calls it an ambition, reasonably confident)
ledger.speaker: Dinesh Taluja
ledger.evidence: Retail 2x EBITDA over three years from Q1 FY27, called an 'ambition' and 'a stretch' (C6). No segment EBITDA is in the facts.

ledger.quote: during next 12 to 15 months our generation capacity will also start coming up.
ledger.statement: Solar generation capacity to start coming up within 12-15 months
ledger.speaker: Karan Suri
ledger.evidence: Polysilicon, ingot, wafer, cell and glass factories are to be commissioned in the 'next few quarters', an open-ended window. By Q2 FY27, cells are guided to 20 GW only in H1 CY2027 (G3). This promise replaces the earlier dates missed under G15 and G16.

ledger.quote: we will have ingot and wafer both these facilities at the giga scale commissioned and fully ramped up to 10-gigawatt peak during the current year.
ledger.statement: Ingot and wafer giga-scale facilities commissioned and ramped to 10 GW peak in FY26
ledger.speaker: Meeting Audio
ledger.evidence: ARPU to rise 4-5% without tariff increases. The inputs have no ARPU data. This is below the 5-6% organic ambition stated one call earlier (G17).

ledger.quote: In next quarter or two, we will again see the entire commissioning of polysilicon.
ledger.statement: Polysilicon plant fully commissioned within one to two quarters
ledger.speaker: Meeting Audio
ledger.evidence: Qualitative pledge not to curtail domestic fuel supply. Nothing in the inputs tests it.

ledger.quote: Organically, if we can improve our ARPU by 5% to 6% a year
ledger.statement: Organic ARPU improvement of 5-6% a year (conditional ambition)
ledger.speaker: Meeting Audio
ledger.evidence: Target to raise one-day installations from over 90% towards 100%. No later figure is in the inputs.

ledger.quote: Aggregate basis will continue to deliver double-digit revenues.
ledger.statement: Retail aggregate revenue growth in double digits
ledger.speaker: Meeting Audio
ledger.evidence: Square footage and store count are expected to grow. The only data point is +1% square footage YoY in Q4 FY26 (C7). Q1 FY27 says dark-store expansion will continue for 9-12 months (C5), but no store or area count follows.

tones.label: confident
tones.why: Reaffirms the retail EBITDA doubling target and dated solar, cell and BESS commissioning, while flagging a retail margin dip.

tones.label: confident
tones.why: On the 2x EBITDA ambition management says We feel reasonably confident, while acknowledging it is a stretch (p2-8-21).

tones.label: confident
tones.why: Reports strong growth and sets dated solar and polysilicon commissioning milestones, with conditional ARPU ambition.

context.text: https://www.ril.com/investors/events-presentations#webcast-sec • Sh V Srikanth 00:00:01 – 00:09:00 (Group Performance) • Sh Anshuman Thakur 00:09:07 – 00:15:37 (Jio Platforms) • Sh Dinesh Taluja 00:15:42 – 00:41:00 (Reliance Retail) • Sh Ashutosh Goyal 00:41:08 - 00:45:01 (FMCG) • Sh Ishan Chatterjee 00:45:13 – 00:50:08 (JioStar) • Sh Srinivas Tuttagunta 00:50:20 – 01:06:49 (Refining & Marketing, O2C) • Sh Amit Chaturvedi 01:07:02 - 01:17:25 (Petrochemicals, O2C) • Sh Sanjay Barman Roy 01:17:35 – 01:21:05 (Exploration & Production) • Q&A Session 01:21:10 - 01:45:05 © Reliance Industries Limited 2020 1 Transcript: PRESENTATION Sh V Srikanth 00:00:01 – 00:09:00 (Group Performance) Starting with the consol presentation. Quick highlights. One was, of course, it is an exceptionally strong quarter in a turbulent world and turbulence in macro, turbulence because of energy disruption. It was an EBITDA of Rs.62,409 Crores, which is 24% up on a year-on- year basis. This is the highest EBITDA that we have declared for consol and simultaneously, the PAT also at close to Rs.30,000 Crores, up 34%. Again, all time high, and with this, we crossed the Rs.50,000 Crores mark as far as PAT is concerned. So, O2C led the charge with EBITDA up 68%. Of course, we benefited from the unprecedented tightness that we saw in energy markets, downstream cracks, fuel cracks, all of them, that is the markets were there, but the operational excellence is something that Srini and Amit will cover. The IPO was absolutely a defining moment, making Jio the second most valuable company. It is particularly nice that it follows Reliance, which is the largest market cap company, and first day listing of almost $137 billion in terms of value. A lot of firsts, which Akash talked about. Largest from size or subscri

Morgan) Lastly, you suggested that you start the installation of modules post monsoon has that started? Company Speaker (Sh Karan Suri) It is still on track. I will not say that the first module has gone, but the project development work is now picked up the pace. The transmission capacity we will start seeing the connectivity by first half or actually Q1 of next year and we will have the necessary modules installed for that. I think we have already given the indication that we will see the revenues for FY2028 from the new energy complex. Questioner (Sanjay Mookim – J.P. Morgan) Thank you.

We have been the world's largest fixed wireless service with 15.1 million connections and with over 78% fixed wireless market share. And we do expect that to ramp up in the coming quarters. And enterprise as well, the differentiated strategy, which is to go beyond just being a connectivity provider to being a full-service provider, becoming the digital gateway for businesses. On connectivity alone with UBR, we have been able to add significantly to the offering that we can give to the larger enterprises.

Also, the gas supplies again in this area was also restricted which meant that the operating rates in the downstream were curtailed and that resulted in low demand for staple and filament. Coming to the situation now, we see that the FTAs, especially the UK FTA which has been signed recently, we expect that it will give a fillip to the textile and the polyester export opportunities. There are new capacities of crackers in China, which are expected to come, although like they have got slightly delayed of late, but they will definitely keep the pressure on the operating rates up.

Company Speaker (Dinesh Taluja) Sure, so I think without getting into specific numbers, we will continue our expansion of our dark store network. At least next 12 months, I think in the next nine to 10 months it will continue. We are focusing on expanding the network going deeper into the markets so that investment will happen. The fixed cost investment is not very high, but when you go capex is not very high, but when you go you set up a dark store, you add the fixed cost and then the order ramp up, etc., happens over a period of time, right, but as I said, we will be quite disciplined.

Dinesh, the guidance that you shared on 2x EBITDA over the next three years, how confident are you and what are the intermediate checkpoints for the next three-year journey that you look at given your investment appetite to ramp up online commerce? That is my first question. Company Speaker (Dinesh Taluja) Sure. It is a target that we are taking that is our ambition we would not be putting it out unless we were confident about it. We feel reasonably confident. Yes, it is a stretch, but we feel confident that we should be able to achieve that.

And as one of the important data points is the fact that we have now 1.6 million orders run rate that is what we are doing, and very much on track to be the second largest QC player. On the FMCG side, the demerger happened on 1st December. And we are at more than 5,000 Crores of turnover, and this is 60% up on a year-on-year basis. A lot of purchases of brands that we have, which we will talk through in those slides. Media continues to do exceptionally well, and even though it was not the sports season and MAUs at about 450 million.

business.what_it_does: Conglomerate spanning oil-to-chemicals (refining and marketing, petrochemicals), exploration and production (KGD6 gas), Jio Platforms (telecom and fixed wireless), Reliance Retail (physical stores, dark-store quick commerce, e-commerce, FMCG), JioStar (media) and a New Energy complex under construction (polysilicon-to-module solar, glass, battery storage). Q2 FY27 consolidated EBITDA was Rs62,409 crore (+24% YoY) and PAT close to Rs30,000 crore (+34%). The inputs give no revenue split by segment.

segments.name: Oil to Chemicals (Refining & Marketing, Petrochemicals)
segments.comment: Q2 FY27 EBITDA up 68% on 'unprecedented tightness' in fuel and downstream cracks. Petrochemicals saw weak polyester demand in Q1 FY27 because of gas restrictions.

segments.name: Jio Platforms
segments.comment: 15.1 million fixed wireless connections with a 78% FWA share. ARPU ambition is 4-5% a year without tariff increases.

segments.name: Reliance Retail (incl. FMCG)
segments.comment: Targets 2x EBITDA over three years, which management calls a stretch. Dark-store expansion continues, while square footage grew only 1% YoY in Q4 FY26.

segments.name: JioStar (media)
segments.comment: Presented as a separate segment on the Q2 FY27 call. The passages give no figures.

segments.name: Exploration & Production
segments.comment: KGD6 gas ceiling price expected to rise by at least USD1 in H2 FY27.

segments.name: New Energy
segments.comment: Module capacity is 6+ GW, with 20 GW of modules and cells due in H1 CY2027 and a 40 GWh BESS facility. First revenue is guided for FY28.

credibility.label: low
credibility.summary: New-energy timelines slip one quarter after another. Ingot and wafer at 10 GW for FY26 was missed, and polysilicon went from 'a quarter or two' to 'next few quarters'; first revenue is now FY28. The ARPU ambition was quietly cut from 5-6% to 4-5%, and the record Q2 FY27 result came from energy-market tightness rather than any guided item.

Retail 2x EBITDA over three years from Q1 FY27, called an 'ambition' and 'a stretch' (C6). No segment EBITDA is in the facts.

Q3 FY26 promised ingot and wafer facilities commissioned and ramped to 10 GW within FY26. After FY26 ended, the Q4 FY26 call still listed ingot and wafer among factories to commission 'in next few quarters' (G9).

ARPU to rise 4-5% without tariff increases. The inputs have no ARPU data. This is below the 5-6% organic ambition stated one call earlier (G17).

Q3 FY26 guided full polysilicon commissioning 'in next quarter or two' (Q4 FY26-Q1 FY27). The Q4 FY26 call loosened this to 'next few quarters' (G9). Neither the Q1 FY27 nor Q2 FY27 passages confirm commissioning, though the window has closed.
Realised gas prices are expected to rise in H2 FY27. H2 is in progress and no realised-price data is given.

Q3 FY26 set an organic ARPU ambition of 5-6% a year. One call later (Q4 FY26), the like-for-like no-tariff figure was 4-5% (G10). That is 100 bps lower at both ends, revised without being flagged as a change.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: An 'exceptionally strong quarter': record EBITDA of Rs62,409 crore (+24%) and PAT close to Rs30,000 crore (+34%).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Q2 FY27 PAT rose 33.8% YoY and revenue 29.8%, with revenue growth accelerating from 10.4% to 29.8% over four quarters. The headline figures match the reported numbers.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: O2C 'led the charge' with EBITDA +68%, attributed to 'operational excellence' as well as tight energy markets.
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Revenue grew 29.8% but EBITDA only 24%, so the consolidated margin fell to 17.1% from 18.0% a year ago. The 3y margin change is only +80 bps (5y -30 bps), and the 3y revenue CAGR is 6.4%. The jump is price-led, not margin-led.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Giga-factories are coming on stream: ingot and wafer at 10 GW in FY26, and polysilicon within 'a quarter or two'.
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Both were still listed as 'next few quarters' after FY26 ended. By Q2 FY27 module capacity is 6+ GW, cells reach 20 GW only in H1 CY2027, no field module was installed, and revenue is pushed to FY28.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Retail will double EBITDA (over three years per Q1 FY27) with double-digit revenue growth.
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: The facts contain no segment numbers. Square footage grew 1% YoY in Q4 FY26, and management itself calls the target 'a stretch'.

bull.point: Record quarter: Q2 FY27 PAT rose 33.8% YoY and EBITDA reached Rs62,409 crore (+24%). Revenue grew 29.8%, the fastest in four quarters, and TTM PAT is INR95,625 crore.
Strong cash generation funds the build-out: 5y FCF was INR98,391 crore with CFO/PAT at 1.9x, and D/E is 0.43.

Dated catalysts: modules from 6+ GW to 20 GW, cells to 20 GW and 40 GWh of BESS, all by H1 CY2027. The KGD6 ceiling price is expected up at least USD1 in H2 FY27, and Jio leads fixed wireless with 15.1 million connections and a 78% share.

bear.point: The quarter rides energy-market tightness: O2C EBITDA rose 68% on cracks, yet the consolidated margin fell to 17.1% from 18.0%. Underlying compounding is slow, with a 3y revenue CAGR of 6.4%, a 3y PAT CAGR of 8.9% and ROCE of 10%.

New-energy dates keep slipping: the 10 GW ingot/wafer target for FY26 was missed, polysilicon went from 'a quarter or two' to 'next few quarters', the first field module was still not installed by Q2 FY27, and revenue is now FY28.

Targets are being softened: the ARPU ambition fell from 5-6% to 4-5%, Retail 2x EBITDA is called 'a stretch', and its horizon reads three years in Q1 FY27 but about two in Q2 FY27. Borrowings are INR4.05 lakh crore, and the cash conversion cycle has widened from 7 to 25 days.

questions: Have the ingot and wafer lines (10 GW, promised within FY26) and the polysilicon plant (promised for Q4 FY26-Q1 FY27) actually been commissioned? What is their output and utilisation today?

Of the Rs62,409 crore Q2 FY27 EBITDA, how much came from cracks above mid-cycle levels? What would the consolidated margin be at normalised cracks, given it already fell to 17.1% from 18.0% a year ago?
Is Retail's 2x EBITDA target three years from Q1 FY27 or two years as framed in Q2 FY27? What base-year EBITDA does it start from, and why was the organic ARPU ambition lowered from 5-6% to 4-5%?
